steps: ECG changes / K ≥6.5: IV CALCIUM gluconate to stabilise the myocardium FIRST.
Shift K intracellularly: IV insulin + dextrose, and nebulised salbutamol.
Remove K: stop K-raising drugs, give a potassium binder; loop diuretic if volume-replete.
Dialysis for refractory/severe hyperkalaemia or established renal failure.
Treat the cause (AKI, drugs — ACEi/ARB/K-sparing, acidosis, rhabdo); recheck K.

drugRefs.regimenLabel: Membrane stabilisation (FIRST if ECG changes / K⁺ ≥6.5)
drugRefs.dose: 10 mL of 10% IV over 5–10 min; repeat if ECG changes persist
drugRefs.freq: repeat every 5–10 min until ECG normalises
drugRefs.why: Stabilises the myocardium; does NOT lower serum K⁺ — give the shift/removal steps alongside.

drugRefs.freq: once, with dextrose; recheck glucose and K⁺
drugRefs.why: Drives K⁺ into cells within 15–30 min. Always co-administer dextrose to prevent hypoglycaemia.

drugRefs.freq: with insulin; monitor glucose for several hours
drugRefs.why: Prevents insulin-induced hypoglycaemia. Omit only if glucose already markedly elevated.
Additional intracellular shift; additive to insulin. Use with caution in ischaemic heart disease.

drugRefs.dose: per product (e.g. SZC 10 g PO TDS acutely)
drugRefs.why: Removes K⁺ from the body (gut). Onset is slower than stabilise/shift measures.

decision.label: IV calcium first if ECG changes / K⁺ ≥6.5

confirm: Raised serum potassium ± ECG changes (peaked T, wide QRS). Treat urgently if K ≥6.5 or ECG changes.
disposition: Admit/monitored area; nephrology if dialysis needed.
